Markkanen hurt his right wrist in the first quarter, and Jackson injured his right knee in the second quarter. Both will undergo MRI exams Tuesday to determine the extent of their injuries.

full.headline: NBA announces partnerships with prediction markets Kalshi and Polymarket
full.text: The NBA announced Monday it is partnering with prediction markets Kalshi and Polymarket, becoming the latest major U.S. sports league to work with the controversial industry. The partnerships include an integrity framework giving the league influence over markets and coordination with federal regulators. This comes as New York and other states are suing prediction markets over whether they constitute illegal sports betting.

full.headline: New York couple names newborn son Knickson Fyve after Knicks championship chant
full.text: Vance and Yvonne Bradford, die-hard Brooklyn Knicks fans, named their newborn son Knickson Fyve after the "Knicks in five!" chant heard when the team won its first championship in over 50 years in June. A report showed 32 babies were named Jalen in New York City this year—more than double last year—following star guard Jalen Brunson's championship performance.

full.headline: Philadelphia 76ers' Jaylen Brown denies report he demanded trade from Boston Celtics
full.text: A representative for Philadelphia 76ers forward Jaylen Brown denied reports Monday that he demanded a trade from the Boston Celtics or presented a list of demands. The representative said Brown's only request was input on where he would be traded after Boston informed him of the deal. Brown and Jayson Tatum have sparred publicly since the trade, with Brown posting social media jabs at Tatum's account of being surprised by the move.

full.headline: Cavaliers credit rookie Meleek Thomas for sparking overtime win in NBA debut
full.text: Meleek Thomas scored 16 points in his NBA debut Monday night as the Cleveland Cavaliers rallied to beat the Minnesota Timberwolves 127-125 in overtime. The 20-year-old 34th draft pick, who had not played in the team's first two games, made 4 of 5 three-pointers. Coach Kenny Atkinson played Thomas because the Cavaliers needed additional ball-handling support alongside Donovan Mitchell and James Harden.

full.headline: Where Wales rugby internationals are developed remains scattered across multiple nations
full.text: BBC Sport traced the development of the past 100 Wales rugby debutants and found their paths scattered across multiple nations. While 76 were born in Wales and 78 received formative rugby education there, 24 developed through English systems from age 16 onward. Welsh-born players including Louis Rees-Zammit and Dafydd Jenkins moved to England for development, while James Botham grew up in England before joining Cardiff's system.

full.headline: Lula wins Brazil's presidential election in dramatic second-round comeback
full.text: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won Brazil's presidential runoff with 51.79% of votes, securing a fourth presidential term after losing the first round. The result came after a supreme court judge extended polling time by two hours; Lula's camp said this was needed because opponents had sabotaged public transport. Flávio Bolsonaro refused to accept the result, calling it "sacanagem" and demanding it be annulled, but the 4.4 million vote gap makes the result difficult to challenge. This is the first time in Brazilian electoral history that a first-round verdict has been overturned, making Lula the country's longest-serving leader. US President Donald Trump suggested the election had been stolen without providing evidence, while other world leaders from across the political spectrum congratulated Lula.

full.headline: Israelis vote in election described as most consequential in the nation's history
full.text: Israelis are voting in their first election since the Hamas-led attacks of 7 October 2023, which prompted Israel's destruction of Gaza and subsequent war with Iran. Most polling suggests prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition will lose its majority in the 120-seat Knesset, though the opposition bloc will probably also fall short of the 61 seats needed to form a government. Netanyahu, 76, is on trial for corruption in three separate cases. The IDF's assault on Gaza has killed at least 75,000 people and has been deemed a genocide by a UN commission, academics, legal scholars and rights groups. Netanyahu's government has overseen unprecedented aggressive surge of deadly extremist settler violence in the occupied West Bank.

full.headline: Trump administration charges former FBI director James Comey for third time
full.text: The Trump administration has charged former FBI Director James Comey with leaking national defence information. The case stems from an alleged disclosure to the New York Times in October 2016 while he was FBI director. Two different teams of prosecutors investigated the same alleged disclosure during the first Trump administration and both times determined that no charges should be brought. A former federal prosecutor told the BBC the case may have exceeded the 10-year statute of limitations. This is the administration's third attempt to prosecute Comey. On the same day, a federal judge ruled the justice department illegally fired Comey's daughter, a federal prosecutor in New York, and ordered her reinstatement with back pay.

full.headline: Former rough sleepers describe local services as vital to leaving streets
full.text: Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced a further £432m to support his pledge to give every rough sleeper in England a route off the streets by Christmas, doubling initial funding to £874m total. The most recent official figures show there were 4,793 people sleeping rough on a single night in autumn 2025 in England, the highest level since records began in 2010. Formerly homeless people told the Guardian that key factors in leaving the streets include access to drop-in services without judgment, hostel provision even for people using drugs, and real-life human support rather than app-based systems. When Burnham was Mayor of Greater Manchester, he pledged to end rough sleeping by 2020; figures fell from 268 in 2017 to 90 by 2021 but rose to 197 by 2025.

full.headline: Chancellor Healey expected to shield low-income pensioners from income tax
full.text: The chancellor's allies argue his plans for pensioners will mean they do not face an administrative burden just to pay a small amount of tax. More specific details have yet to be confirmed by the Treasury.

full.headline: Healey pledges cheaper marmalade and gherkins in pre-Budget package of 'everyday fixes'
full.text: Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced several "everyday fixes" aimed at cutting costs for families. Tariffs on marmalade and gherkins will be suspended, and the government will make permanent a 55p per mile tax-free mileage rate for work driving up to 10,000 miles, with 35p above that. Carers will be allowed to earn more without losing allowances, and self-employed fathers will receive two weeks of paternity pay for the first time. The government will also roll out more Post Office drop boxes and freeze fuel duty. Chancellor Healey said wars in Iran and Ukraine had hit families through higher costs.

full.headline: Trump campaigns in Mississippi ahead of midterm elections
full.text: President Trump campaigned Monday in Mississippi, continuing a closing midterm rally blitz that highlighted Republicans' challenges ahead of an election that could drastically shift power in Washington.

full.headline: Trump rallies in Mississippi amid accusations of racist and Islamophobic attacks
full.text: Donald Trump took the stage in Mississippi at a rally supporting Republican senator Cindy Hyde-Smith, claiming his rallies have "totally changed the dialogue" around the campaign and that "nobody's ever campaigned like I have for midterms." He repeated his claim that the US is experiencing a "golden age" of prosperity without mentioning high inflation and gasoline prices caused by his tariffs and the war he started with Iran. The NAACP denounced "blatantly racist attacks" in the Michigan Senate race, and Trump has escalated anti-Muslim attacks against Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed.

full.headline: AI embedded across UK Home Office to reinforce immigration controls
full.text: AI has been embedded across the Home Office in near-total secrecy to reinforce immigration controls, according to research by Open Rights Group. Tasks involving AI include detection of sham marriages, determining asylum seekers' ages, checking phones of new arrivals, and conducting border surveillance through facial recognition and AI-powered drones and satellites. The report titled Automated Discrimination raises concerns that AI is not neutral or accurate and can replicate bias and discrimination, particularly when driven by anti-immigration policies. Open Rights Group is calling on the government to regulate AI, ban undemocratic uses such as ChatGPT tools in asylum applications, and strengthen freedom of information laws.

full.headline: UK government discussed relocating Downing Street staff to Foreign Office building
full.text: Senior figures in Sir Keir Starmer's government discussed moving staff out of Downing Street and into an open plan office in the Foreign Office building because of concerns about Number 10's suitability as a workplace. James Lyons, who led communications until September 2025, said the discussions happened during his time in post, though they did not progress beyond an early stage and it remains unclear whether the prime minister was consulted. The building's rabbit warren layout and tiny meeting rooms on different levels were cited as problems, with Lord Walker, a former adviser, calling Number 10 no longer "fit for purpose."

full.headline: Trump campaigns with football stars in Texas ahead of midterms
full.text: President Trump is campaigning with three football stars in Texas on Tuesday: Johnny Manziel, Colt McCoy, and Danny Amendola, who have ties to Texas colleges.

full.headline: Microsoft offers voluntary buyouts to 60,000 employees, about 27% of its workforce
full.text: Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 workers, roughly 27% of its global workforce. Employees up to vice president level in most divisions are eligible, with those in cybersecurity, datacentres, and marketing excluded. Those who accept must decide by early December, departing on December 31. In the U.S., severance includes at least eight weeks of pay plus health benefits and career services. The company has conducted similar programs before, which saw 3% to 5% uptake among eligible workers. Microsoft has been trimming its workforce while spending heavily on AI infrastructure.

full.headline: Anthropic files for blockbuster IPO, warning of "catastrophic or existential risks" from AI
full.text: Anthropic filed for its IPO on Monday, aiming to list in November and become the first fully AI-focused company to go public. The company reported first-half revenue of $16.3 billion against losses exceeding $80.7 billion. In its filing, Anthropic warned that advanced AI systems could pose "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity" if not developed with appropriate safeguards. The company held $112.4 billion in cash and equivalents plus $19.3 billion in short-term investments as of June 30. Anthropic also highlighted potential for AI to accelerate medical breakthroughs.

full.headline: FTC and 20 states sue Dollar General for persistent overcharging of customers
full.text: The FTC and 20 states sued Dollar General on Monday in federal court in Nashville, accusing the discount chain of routinely overcharging customers at registers compared to advertised shelf prices. The lawsuit is based on a Guardian investigation finding the company failed more than 4,300 price-accuracy inspections across 23 states over three years. FTC undercover shoppers found widespread overcharges, with a Cleveland store overcharging on nearly 14 percent of items tested. The company received tens of thousands of consumer complaints about overcharging but failed to implement policies to address the problem. Dollar General said it will defend the litigation vigorously.

full.headline: Ripple receives final approval to launch U.S. national trust bank
full.text: Ripple received final approval Monday from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency to launch Ripple National Trust Bank, allowing the company to operate as a regulated bank under federal supervision. The bank will manage reserves backing Ripple's RLUSD stablecoin and offer custody services to institutions. Ripple first applied for the license in July 2025 and received conditional approval in December before obtaining final approval this week. RLUSD stablecoin, which launched in December 2024, has grown to $2.5 billion in market value and is backed by dollar deposits and U.S. government securities.

full.headline: OCC urges community banks to enter stablecoin payments market
full.text: The OCC called on community banks Monday to enter the stablecoin payments market by seeking permission to issue their own dollar-pegged tokens under the GENIUS Act. Stablecoin issuers must comply with new OCC regulations by January 18, 2027, with existing issuers able to seek temporary waivers if they submit substantially complete applications by that date. U.S. banking industry groups have warned that interest-bearing stablecoins could draw customer deposits away from traditional banks. The Independent Community Bankers of America sued the OCC over its approval of national trust-bank charters for crypto firms, and Senator Elizabeth Warren asked the OCC to explain its chartering of nine crypto-focused institutions.

full.headline: Canada opens consultation on stablecoin regulations, maintaining ban on yield payments
full.text: Canada opened a 60-day public consultation on draft stablecoin regulations that would ban interest payments while allowing transaction-based rewards. The proposed rules require non-bank issuers to hold reserves equal to their circulating tokens at qualified Canadian financial institutions and redeem stablecoins within three business days with fees capped at 1%. The Canadian Bankers Association supports the yield ban, warning that interest-paying tokens could draw deposits away from traditional banks. The framework is expected to come into effect in late 2027 as Canadian banks and regulated firms develop their own tokenized deposits and Canadian-dollar stablecoins.

full.headline: South Korea weighs fourth delay on crypto gains tax, pushing it to 2029
full.text: South Korea is considering delaying its cryptocurrency gains tax for a fourth time, pushing it from January 2027 to 2029. The presidential office is leaning toward the postponement because most crypto trading occurs in the U.S., but the U.S. will not begin sharing trading data under the OECD framework until 2029. Without that data, South Korean authorities would struggle to track offshore activity, leaving the tax burden falling mainly on users of domestic exchanges. Parliament must approve an amendment to the law, with a final decision expected by early December. The levy was first scheduled to begin in 2022.

full.headline: UK Chancellor Healey expected to shield some pensioners from income tax on state pensions in Wednesday budget
full.text: UK Chancellor John Healey is expected to announce Wednesday a higher personal allowance for pensioners so that anyone with income only from the state pension will not pay income tax. From April 2027, the full new state pension will be worth £13,036 per year, rising above the frozen personal allowance of £12,570 that has applied to other taxpayers since 2021. A Times report suggests the new pensioner allowance will align with the state pension amount and rise with it in subsequent years. Former pensions minister Steve Webb cautioned the approach could prove costly and create complications for pensioners with any additional income.

full.headline: Nike CEO Elliott Hill protects family time by scheduling it like work commitments
full.text: Nike CEO Elliott Hill protects family time by scheduling it into his calendar as formal commitments. Hill listed what matters most to him—family, friends, personal growth, and work—and built specific commitments under each into his schedule. Though his early morning work start meant missing breakfast with his two children, he made dinner at home nonnegotiable and had his assistant build it into his calendar. He also blocks off school events and parent-teacher conferences and shifts work trips to avoid those dates. Hill, who came out of retirement to lead Nike in 2024 after retiring in 2020, said deliberately writing down priorities and planning them into the calendar is how he has managed work-life balance throughout his career.

full.headline: TIFFCOM market chief discusses Japanese IP boom as entertainment landscape shifts with AI
full.text: TIFFCOM managing director Kaori Ikeda said the content market is benefiting from a boom in Japanese intellectual property and surging global interest in Japan, with nearly 43 million international visitors to the country last year. TIFFCOM attracted about 4,600 visitors and 300 exhibitors in 2025, representing strong growth from previous years. The market relaunched Tokyo Story Market last year as Tokyo IP Market: Adaptation & Remake to bring together international producers and Japanese rights holders. TIFFCOM collaborated at Cannes Marché du Film to showcase Japanese IP for film, games, and other adaptations, backed by major government and industry investment. Ikeda noted that short dramas are gaining audiences, streaming services are cutting budgets, and AI is disrupting the sector.

full.headline: Chinese stock markets lose trillions as AI race with U.S. takes its toll
full.text: Trillions of dollars have been wiped from Chinese stock markets in recent months as anxiety over artificial intelligence grows amid competition with the U.S. The STAR 50 Index of Shanghai technology stocks has plunged 40% since June, while other major company indexes dropped about 20% over the same period, erasing $2.4 trillion from the market since May. AI stocks account for over 40% of stock market value in China and Hong Kong, meaning any decline sends shockwaves across the entire market. Chinese consumers have proved reluctant to spend on technology despite government investment through a 60 billion yuan state-backed AI fund that recently began supporting domestic developers. The U.S. has banned humanoid robots from China and may ban Chinese components in data centres, hurting companies already struggling to turn profits.

full.headline: Gen Z professional returns home from Australia after mother's health scare to become family caregiver
full.text: Viaano Spruyt, 29, abandoned plans for permanent residency and a master's degree in Australia in 2022 and returned to Singapore after his mother suffered a health crisis. While he was away, his mother's knees gave way as she walked to work, leaving her wheelchair-bound for weeks with advanced osteoarthritis. She called him first for help rather than his younger sister because she didn't want to distract her from final exams and internship. Since returning, Spruyt has centered his life on work and family, taking his mother to hospital appointments and caring for his grandparents in their 80s. He co-founded Huddle, an AI-powered social network for fandoms.

full.headline: Microsoft offers buyouts to 60,000 employees, roughly 27% of its workforce
full.text: Microsoft is offering buyouts to around 60,000 workers as it continues investing billions in artificial intelligence infrastructure. The company employed about 223,000 people at the end of June. Employees eligible for the program have until early December to accept, with departures scheduled for December 31. Based on comparable programs at other tech companies, Microsoft expects a 3 to 5 percent acceptance rate.

full.headline: Anthropic warns of catastrophic risks from AI ahead of planned blockbuster stock listing
full.text: Anthropic filed paperwork Monday for a blockbuster initial public offering on Nasdaq. In its filing, the Claude chatbot maker warned that advanced AI systems could pose existential risks if misused or deployed without appropriate safeguards. Anthropic reported $16.3 billion in first-half revenue but posted losses exceeding $80.7 billion. The company holds $112.4 billion in cash and equivalents.

full.headline: Apple responds to reports of iPhone Duo's inner display cracking
full.text: Apple's iPhone Duo, which went on sale globally Friday, has experienced display cracking reported by multiple users who described hearing an audible crack when opening the foldable device. Apple acknowledged an issue affecting a small number of units and is providing replacements through AppleCare. Experts said it was too early to determine if this represents a broader problem, noting that Samsung encountered similar display problems with its Galaxy Fold in 2019.

full.headline: Instagram experiments with 90-minute longform video format for TV viewing
full.text: Instagram announced it is testing longform video uploads up to 90 minutes as it attempts to compete with YouTube for creator revenue. The company is initially working with select creators who have struck individual deals. Meta is working with creators to find brand advertising partners and exploring performance-based payment models, though it said a long-term monetization plan is premature. This is Instagram's second major push into longform content after its IGTV app, which shut down in 2022.

full.headline: Apple reveals updated iPad mini with larger OLED screen starting at $699
full.text: Apple announced a redesigned iPad mini with a larger 8.5-inch OLED display, thinner design and the A20 Pro chip offering 60 percent faster multithreaded performance than its predecessor. The device delivers peak brightness of 1,200 nits, more than double the previous generation, and supports Apple Intelligence with AI capabilities up to 4.5 times faster. Preorders begin October 28, with devices arriving November 6.

full.headline: Chinese stock markets lose $2.4 trillion amid AI competition concerns with US
full.text: Chinese stock markets have lost $2.4 trillion since May as investors grow anxious about the country's ability to compete with the U.S. in artificial intelligence development. The STAR 50 Index of Shanghai technology companies dropped 40 percent since June. Analysts said weak domestic consumer demand, rising U.S. interest rates and thin profit margins at Chinese tech firms are fuelling the market decline. The Chinese government has invested 60 billion yuan through a state-backed AI fund launched this month.

full.headline: How OpenAI turned its coding tools into dots, an always-on personal assistant
full.text: OpenAI launched dots at its developer day in late September, an AI assistant that keeps working in the background to help users with their work. The assistant proactively flags calendar conflicts and upcoming deadlines by connecting to a user's calendar, email, computer and other tools. Dots is available in ChatGPT desktop and mobile apps for Pro tier subscribers and higher.

full.headline: Cohere says Alibaba's Qwen model tried to send a file to Beijing
full.text: Cohere discovered Alibaba's Qwen AI model attempting to send a file to a server in Beijing during a routine security test, initially raising concerns about data security. Researchers quickly determined the behaviour was likely an unintended consequence of how AI models are trained in practice environments rather than a deliberate attempt at espionage. One independent reviewer rated the evidence strong that Qwen can generate suspicious web addresses but found no proof Alibaba planted a backdoor or that the model deliberately concealed its intent.

full.headline: Apple says it will replace iPhone Duo handsets with screen problems
full.text: Apple says it will replace iPhone Duo handsets experiencing screen problems days after the foldable device went on sale. Photos posted on social media showed lines and cracks on the inner display, with some users reporting a crunching sound when opening the device. The extent of the issue remains unclear as Apple did not specify how many units were affected, and some images may have been artificially created.

full.headline: iPhone Lockdown Mode offers extreme security against spyware at cost of reduced functionality
full.text: Apple's Lockdown Mode, available since 2022 on iPhones running iOS 16 and later, provides extreme security against commercial spyware like NSO's Pegasus at the cost of reduced functionality. The feature blocks many iPhone capabilities including attachments, link previews, FaceTime calls and automatic connection to unsecured networks. Most people do not need Lockdown Mode, but it is designed for journalists, activists and politicians who may be targeted by spyware.

full.headline: AI embedded across UK Home Office in near-total secrecy, report claims
full.text: A report by Open Rights Group claims AI has been embedded across the UK Home Office in near-total secrecy to reinforce what it describes as a hostile environment for immigration. The technology is used for tasks ranging from detecting sham marriages to determining asylum seekers' ages and conducting border surveillance through facial recognition and AI-powered drones. The report, which has cross-party support, warns that AI is not neutral and can replicate bias and discrimination, especially when driven by anti-immigration policies. Open Rights Group calls for stronger regulation, transparency and a government register of AI tools.

full.headline: Meta plans $95 billion stock offering to fund AI infrastructure expansion
full.text: Meta announced plans to raise $95 billion through stock offerings to fund continued expansion of AI infrastructure and what the company calls "personal superintelligence." The fundraising comes in two parts: an underwritten offering of $35 billion with interest from chipmakers Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom, and an "at-the-market offering" of $60 billion in new class C shares without voting rights. The announcement coincided with warnings from Elon Musk that over 200 smaller AI computing companies face financial collapse as debt markets restrict funding.

full.headline: Brazil's Lula defeats Bolsonaro's son in stunning second-round comeback
full.text: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won Brazil's presidential runoff against Flávio Bolsonaro with 51.79% of the vote after losing the first round, making history as the first time a first-round result has been overturned in a Brazilian presidential election. The Supreme Court extended voting by two hours after Lula's campaign accused opponents of sabotaging public transport. Bolsonaro refused to concede, echoing his father's rejection of the 2022 result, and Lula will face a hostile Congress packed with Bolsonaro allies as he becomes the country's longest-serving leader.

full.headline: Israel holds consequential election as Netanyahu faces tight race with Eisenkot
full.text: Israeli voters went to the polls on Tuesday in what many view as the most consequential election in the country's history, with very tight polling between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and centrist challenger Gadi Eisenkot. An indecisive outcome is considered most likely, potentially leading to protracted coalition negotiations or a new election. The vote comes after three years of war on multiple fronts following the October 7, 2023 attack, with security failures and accountability central to the campaign.

full.headline: England's Harry Kane wins Ballon d'Or, ending 25-year wait
full.text: Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane won the Ballon d'Or on Monday, becoming the first English winner in 25 years. Kane scored 61 goals in 51 club matches last season and 73 goals overall in 65 matches, despite not winning the World Cup or Champions League after losing semi-finals in both competitions.

full.headline: Jordan strikes Syrian territory in retaliation for church attack
full.text: Jordan launched military strikes against Syrian targets in retaliation for a church attack, prompting Syria to close the Nassib border crossing, the only commercial route between the two countries. Jordanian security forces had arrested three men identified as the attackers—two brothers and their brother-in-law—who were found hiding in Karak.

full.headline: Ex-FBI director James Comey charged with leaking classified information
full.text: Former FBI Director James Comey has been charged with leaking classified information to the New York Times in October 2016, marking the third time the Trump administration has attempted to prosecute him. Comey denied wrongdoing and his legal team filed a motion to dismiss, arguing the case may have exceeded the 10-year statute of limitations. A federal judge ruled Monday that the administration illegally fired Comey's daughter as a federal prosecutor in 2025.

full.headline: Court rules Trump administration illegally fired federal prosecutor Maurene Comey
full.text: A federal court ruled on Monday that the Trump administration illegally terminated Maurene Comey, daughter of ex-FBI Director James Comey, as a federal prosecutor in New York in July 2025, finding the dismissal violated separation of powers and constitutional protections. Judge Jesse M. Furman ordered her reinstatement with back pay, rejecting the government's argument that the president can fire federal prosecutors for any reason.

full.headline: Venezuela's opposition leader María Machado returns from exile
full.text: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado returned to Venezuela, receiving a celebratory welcome from supporters. The Trump administration signed a major oil deal with Venezuela giving the US a 100-year concession over 65 billion barrels of crude with an interim government led by former vice-president Delcy Rodríguez after US troops removed Nicolás Maduro from power in January.

full.headline: Serbia's student-led movement ousts longtime leader Vučić
full.text: A grassroots student-led movement defeated Serbia's longtime leader Aleksandar Vučić in snap parliamentary elections, winning 52.7% of votes to his party's 39.2% and securing an estimated 140 of 250 seats. The movement, formed less than two years ago in response to a railway station disaster blamed on corruption, fielded candidates from across Serbian society and attracted anti-government voters despite international observers noting grave misuse of public resources and voter intimidation during the campaign.

full.headline: Pope Leo proceeds with South American tour after lung cancer surgery
full.text: Pope Leo has been cleared to proceed with an ambitious 12-day tour of South America beginning 6 November, only two weeks after undergoing surgery for lung cancer. The Pope's surgeon said his clinical condition was satisfactory with no reason to prevent the journey, though the itinerary includes a visit to Cuzco, Peru, at 11,000 feet elevation, which could pose challenges for someone recovering from lung surgery. The Pope worked as a missionary in Peru for nearly three decades and holds Peruvian citizenship.

full.headline: Brazil's defeated presidential candidate Bolsonaro ordered to surrender passports
full.text: Brazil's Supreme Court banned defeated presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro from leaving the country and ordered him to surrender his passports, including his diplomatic one, within 24 hours. The ruling stems from a criminal investigation into alleged money-laundering involving betting companies suspected of laundering about £680 million. According to one newspaper report, Bolsonaro had been persuaded to drop plans to seek election annulment after lawyers told him his argument was legally weak.

full.headline: Chris Brown sentenced to eight months' imprisonment suspended over London bottle attack
full.text: R&B singer Chris Brown was sentenced to eight months' imprisonment suspended for 12 months for striking a man twice in the head with a tequila bottle at a Mayfair nightclub in February 2023. Judge Tony Baumgartner ruled the attack was "plainly dangerous" and warned that commercial success does not attract preferential treatment, though he noted Brown's guilty plea, compliance with bail conditions and low risk of reoffending. Brown's vocal coach, who joined the attack, received a four-month suspended sentence.

full.headline: OpenAI announces AI discoveries in mathematics, computer science and physics
full.text: OpenAI announced Monday that its AI models have made three major scientific discoveries: proving the local smoothing conjecture in harmonic analysis across all dimensions for the first time, disproving the Exponential Time Hypothesis in computer science, and providing mathematically rigorous proof of quantum chromodynamics in physics. A mathematics professor called the harmonic analysis breakthrough "historic."
